pr.title: Enable DestinationPropagation by default
pr.description:
This PR proposes to perform destination propagation on MIR. Most of the pass was fully rewritten by @JakobDegen in rust-lang/rust#96451. 

This pass is quite heavy, as it needs to perform and save the results of a full liveness dataflow analysis. This accounts for ~50% of the pass' runtime. 

Perf sees a few decent savings in later llvm passes, but also sizeable régressions when there are no savings to balance this pass' runtime.

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.originalLogic: RenameReturnPlace (deleted by this PR) looked for a simple assignment of a whole local into `_0`, required that `_0` was not read before `Return`, and then renamed all uses of that local to `_0`. Its documented eligibility was: "The return place must not be read prior to the `Return` terminator." and "A simple assignment of a whole local to the return place (e.g., `_0 = _1`) must be the only definition of the return place reaching the `Return` terminator." The implementation scanned backward from each `Return` block along single-predecessor chains for `if lhs.as_local() == Some(mir::RETURN_PLACE)`, Nop'd the copy and the source local's storage statements, ignored the implicit Return use, and copied the source local's LocalDecl/debuginfo onto `_0`. It did not require the source local to be dead or unchanged after the copy.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For MIR of the form `_2 = copy _1; _0 = copy _2; _2 = const 'b'; return`, the old pass accepted `_2` as the returned local and renamed all `_2` uses/definitions to `_0`, producing the wrong `_0 = copy _1; _0 = const 'b'; return`. The later write to `_2` became a write to the return place, so a return value that should still be the copied argument becomes `'b'`. The historical test pins this wrong behavior with `// FIXME: This is wrong:` and `// CHECK-NEXT: _0 = const 'b';`. This is the old RenameReturnPlace rewrite, not the fixed implementation; the replacement pass's decoded regression output is `nop; _0 = copy _1; _1 = const 'b'; return`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR function bodies, especially `#[custom_mir]`, post-inlining MIR, or other constructed MIR, where a local is copied into the return place and then written again before `Return`. The bug is about post-copy overwrites of the source local and its overlapping live range with `_0`; borrowing restrictions are a separate constraint and are not the cause of #111005.
analysis.summary: This PR enables DestinationPropagation by default at MIR optimization level 2 and removes the unsound RenameReturnPlace pass (#111005). The reusable correctness lesson is that an NRVO-style "local is copied into the return place" pattern is unsafe unless the source local has no later overlapping write: renaming all later uses/definitions to `_0` can redirect a post-copy write into the return place and change the returned value. DestinationPropagation must preserve such later writes to the source local, as shown by the corrected `_1 = const 'b'` output.
analysis.trigger: A local copied into `_0` is written again after that copy but before `Return`. The old backward eligibility scan still accepts it because it only looks for a `_0 = local` assignment reaching Return and does not check for later writes to `local`; renaming all uses/definitions of `local` to `_0` then changes the return value. `// This is a miscompilation, #111005 to track` documents this case.
preconditions: MIR contains an assignment of an unprojected local to `_0` (`if lhs.as_local() == Some(mir::RETURN_PLACE)`) found by the backward scan, and `_0` is not read before `Return`.
The source local is a Temp, is the same across all return blocks, and is redefined/overwritten after the `_0 = local` assignment but before `Return`.
The old pass is enabled under its historical gate `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0 && sess.opts.unstable_opts.unsound_mir_opts`; this PR deletes it because it is `// unsound: #111005`.

For the replacement-path regression, DestinationPropagation is enabled at `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 2` and runs in the new pipeline slot after `DeadStoreElimination::Final` instead of `RenameReturnPlace`.
pitfalls: The 'only definition of the return place reaching Return' check is not a liveness/no-overlap check; the backward scan stops at the nearest `_0 = local` and can miss a later redefinition of `local` after that assignment.

Renaming every use and every StorageLive/StorageDead of the source local to `_0` is unsound when the source local is written after the return-place copy; the rename must not move that later write onto `_0`.
The return place is special: any later `_0 = ...` before `Return` clobbers the value that was copied in, so `_0` must not be treated as an ordinary destination for a still-live source local.

Borrowing restrictions are separate from the #111005 post-copy overwrite. In `nrvo_borrowed`, the new expected MIR retains `debug buf => _2;`, `_6 = &mut _2;`, and `_0 = copy _2;`, whereas the deleted NRVO output had `debug buf => _0;`, `_6 = &mut _0;`, and no return copy; do not use the shared `nrvo_*` name to argue DestinationPropagation is wrong.

The pass was moved from before final simplification to after `DeadStoreElimination::Final` while replacing `RenameReturnPlace`, and its gate changed from `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 3` to `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 2`; MIR-dump test names, pass annotations, and CHECK patterns must be updated together.
A retained test name or old FIXME comment does not establish that the replacement pass is incorrect; compare the actual assignments in the decoded before/after MIR.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/` test using `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation` and `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime", phase = "initial")]` to construct `_2 = copy _1; _0 = copy _2; _2 = const 'b'; return`. Pin the rewritten MIR so the return copy remains `_0 = copy _1;` and the later write is `_1 = const 'b';`, explicitly rejecting the old wrong `_0 = const 'b';`. Pair it with a control MIR differing only in whether the source local is overwritten after the return-place copy, so the two outputs isolate the transformation. Keep panic-abort and panic-unwind EMIT_MIR diffs, and inspect MIR dumps at `-Zmir-opt-level=2` to cover the new default enablement. No compiler was built here, so this is a patch-derived test plan, not an execution result.
